Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

structure noun

the way the parts of something are arranged

also make-up, framework, sentence structure, structural

classical

Cic. N.D. 1.47: conpositiō membrōrum, the edition’s spelling
Cic. Fin. 3.74: compositiō disciplīnae (Lewis & Short)

compositiō, compositiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a putting together; arrangement, structure

Other words

  • fabrica, fabricae f. — structure, design (of something skilfully made)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.127: hanc nātūrae tam dīligentem fabricam; M-O s.v. organize: structure

  • strūctūra, strūctūrae f. — an arrangement, a structure (of words)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 33: verbōrum quasi strūctūra (Lewis & Short)

    In Cicero only as a figure, with quasi; freely in later prose (Lewis & Short).

  • cōnfōrmātiō, cōnfōrmātiōnis f. — shape, build, structure

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 1.47: cōnfōrmātiō līniāmentōrum

  • ōrdō, ōrdinis m. — order, arrangement

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Col. 12.2.4: dispositiōne atque ōrdine

Examples

  • quae conpositiō membrōrum, quae cōnfōrmātiō līniāmentōrum, quae figūra, quae speciēs hūmāna potest esse pulchrior?

    what structure of limbs, what shape of features, what figure or appearance could be more beautiful than the human?Cic. N.D. 1.47

  • hanc nātūrae tam dīligentem fabricam imitāta est hominum verēcundia

    this careful design of nature has been copied by human modestyCic. Off. 1.127

  • nihil esse pulchrius in omnī ratiōne vītae dispositiōne atque ōrdine

    that in every walk of life nothing is finer than arrangement and orderCol. 12.2.4

See also structure, order, system.
